DataPropertyAssertion.Literal: Legacy OWL 1 description-logic tests whose current result differs. Not yet triaged; some cases may reflect OWL 1/RDF-based semantics rather than a defect.
RDF-based equality/disjointness and negative-assertion idioms whose direct-semantics form is not unique. To be triaged.
OWL 2 features that are not handled or not handled correctly: bottom object/data properties, keys, owl:rational and negative assertions.
Datatype value-space differences: datatype complements, float discreteness, infinities, signed zero and integer/real equality.
Disjoint data properties are not enforced, so the test is reported consistent instead of inconsistent.
rdf:XMLLiteral whitespace semantics differ from the expected result.
The OWL/XML parser maps HasKey to the unsupported-node handler, so key axioms are silently ignored.

Fixed. The engine already returned the left-join rows; the XML serializers wrote a non-standard <unbound/> binding element for an unbound variable. Unbound variables are now omitted from the binding, as required by SPARQL Results XML. Guards: kt:sparql-optional and kt:sparql-lang-select-optional.
SELECT with UNION returns no rows although both branches have matches.
A FILTER comparing an individual to a constant does not terminate; the test is capped at 5 seconds.

Fixed by passing the datatype of an explicitly typed xsd:string literal on as its full IRI instead of the QName xsd:string, which the literal normaliser could not resolve. The test is a regular test again.
A query for the declared classes or properties of the ontology answers nothing, so an ASK for the declaration of a class is false.

A triple pattern with a variable predicate and a constant object segfaulted in the Redland/Rasqal sub-query resolving because the sub-query had no answer result when it was initialised. The crash is guarded now (the sub-query contributes no statements), but such queries still answer nothing.

An ASK about a data property value of a named subject crashes while the instance entailment result is processed (the query has no processing linker). The SELECT half was fixed separately: it answered no rows because the data literal base item resolved the query individual only in the expression mapping of the ontology; the item now resolves it by name through the ontology string mapping and answers the asserted value and values entailed through sub-properties. The ASK test is capped at 5 seconds.

Data property value queries (with a named subject and with a variable subject) answer the asserted values, including the values of sub-properties, and values that are only entailed: a value of an owl:hasValue restriction on the individual as well as a value that is derived from the TBox (for example B <= C and C <= (dp hasValue v) for an instance of B). The values are provided by the data literal realization of the individual, which is computed on demand from the asserted data, the asserted concepts and the backend cache labels. Non-deterministically derived values are only answered when they hold in the deterministic part of the realization.

A data value that only follows from a non-deterministic branch (for example one branch of a union or an at-most restriction) is treated as a candidate and verified lazily. The realizing item queues a satisfiability test of the individual together with the negated value (individual and not(SOME(dataProperty,{value}))) and caches the result per (individual, data property, value); only values whose negation is unsatisfiable are published. The verification uses temporary SOME concepts in the ontology of the realizing item, so no answerer state is needed. Deterministic values, including TBox-derived hasValue and minimum cardinality values, are answered without a test.

A minimum cardinality restriction with a literal-only data range (DataMinCardinality 1 over DataOneOf "atleast") forces the data value. The label scan now also extracts the literal of the data range of an at-least restriction with cardinality one (CCATLEAST with CCATALITERAL operand), so the value is answered; the candidate verification covers branch-dependent variants.

Fixed. The existential interpretation remains config-gated (Konclude.Answering.InterpretNonAnswerIndividualVariablesAsAnonymousVariables); the single-variable boolean ASK reduction is skipped so named witnesses work with the default config. A closed ASK is answered directly from the conjunction of its boolean sub-queries, and non-closed sub-queries use query-local placeholders for hidden individual variables while preserving direct-result streaming. The regular resolver path is covered by the *-regular tests with Konclude.Answering.ClosedAskDirectBooleanAnswering=false. Regression guards include kt:sparql-ask-class-assertion, kt:sparql-ask-complex, kt:sparql-ask-anonymous-woman, kt:sparql-ask-anonymous-child, kt:sparql-ask-anonymous-woman-child, kt:sparql-ask-anonymous-man, kt:sparql-select-anonymous-woman and kt:sparql-select-hidden-anonymous-join.

A variable-predicate query over constant individuals (for example SELECT ?p { sp:alice ?p sp:bob } or SELECT ?d ?v { sp:alice ?d ?v }) answers empty. The parser classifies the pattern as an object-property or data-property SCHEMA query (property hierarchy) instead of a fact query over the known subject/object, so the role/data-property variable never becomes a binding. The object-property path is the allObjPropVars branch; the data-property path is the allDataPropVars branch in CSPARQLRedlandRasqalReasoningBGPQueryParser::generateBGPBasedSubQueries. Affects kt:sparql-select-role-variable and kt:sparql-select-data-variable.

Fixed. Completion graph caching missed an equality between two nominals that is forced by a qualified minimum cardinality. In cgc-l-nominal-cardinality-ontology.owl.xml, A is {a0,a1} and B is {a0,a4}; B is a subclass of (at least 2 r.B), B is a subclass of (A or C), (some r.C) is a subclass of D and C is disjoint from D, which forces a4 = a1 and A = B. In the deterministic graph the successors of a4 and a0 are blocked during the deterministic expansion preprocessing (processing blocked) by one successor of a0, but they were not registered at that blocker. The consistency test woke them through its processing queues; a later test starts from the deterministic graph without these queue entries, so when it merged the rebuilt blocker into a4 the successors of a4 were never processed, never chose a0 or a4, and the cardinality conflict was not found. Processing-blocked nodes are now registered at their blocker (detectIndividualNodeBlockedStatus) and woken by eliminiateBlockedIndividuals, a woken node that is presumed cached is tested for caching again, and a node that the cached graph pruned is no longer accepted as a cache witness (CCompletionGraphCacheHandler::testCompletionGraphCached). Guards: kt:cgc-l-a-not-b, kt:cgc-l-a1-not-a4, kt:cgc-l-classification (four caching configurations) and the negative controls kt:cgc-l-a1-a4 and kt:cgc-l-consistent.

Fixed. When a node lost its completion graph caching, the reactivation followed the nodes that the cached model had merged into it, but not the node that it had been merged into. In cgc-n2-three-nominal-ontology.owl.xml the cached model merged a4 into a2 and a5 into a1; a test that adds a concept to a4 rebuilt a4, while a2 stayed cached with the merge of a4 in its cached state, so the a2 choice was never redone and ({a4} and not A) and ({a4} and {a5}) were answered satisfiable. The same gap made the classification of cgc-n1-exact-cardinality-ontology.owl.xml under reduced saturation miss B below A. CCompletionGraphCacheHandler::getReactivationIndividuals now also reactivates (forced) the cached representative of a node that loses its caching. The classification additionally tested {a4} and {a1}, where the nominal a4 is merged into a test node that already carries the nominal a1; a nominal that is merged into another nominal node did not lose its caching, so mergeIndividualNodeInto now clears the caching of every merged nominal. Guards: kt:cgc-n2-a4-not-a, kt:cgc-n2-a4-a5 and kt:cgc-n2-classification in Tests/cases/cgc-known-n2 (default-config, delayed-caching-reactivation, no-backjumping).

Fixed. When a node lost its completion graph caching, the reactivation followed the nodes that the cached model had merged into it, but not the node that it had been merged into. In cgc-n2-three-nominal-ontology.owl.xml the cached model merged a4 into a2 and a5 into a1; a test that adds a concept to a4 rebuilt a4, while a2 stayed cached with the merge of a4 in its cached state, so the a2 choice was never redone and ({a4} and not A) and ({a4} and {a5}) were answered satisfiable. The same gap made the classification of cgc-n1-exact-cardinality-ontology.owl.xml under reduced saturation miss B below A. CCompletionGraphCacheHandler::getReactivationIndividuals now also reactivates (forced) the cached representative of a node that loses its caching. Guards: kt:cgc-n1-classification in Tests/cases/cgc-known-n1 (reduced-saturation).

Fixed. Differential fuzzing (caching on against caching off and HermiT) found four more cases in which a node kept its cached state although a node it shares that state with was rebuilt. (1) Nodes merged into a node through a chain of merges (v into a1, a1 into a0) were not found, only nodes whose final representative is the node (cgc-o1). (2) A node that is taken from the reactivation queue as a forced reactivation did not pass the reactivation on to the nodes merged with it (cgc-o1, cgc-o3); it now calls CCompletionGraphCacheHandler::getMergeDependentReactivationIndividuals, which covers the representative, the merged blockable nodes and the merged nominals but not the connection neighbours (the full caching loss there made the roberts classification about six times slower). (3) CIndividualReactivationProcessingQueue::insertReactivationIndiviudal let a later re-check request turn an earlier forced entry of the same node into a re-check (cgc-o2). (4) The classification message analyser accepted the deterministic concepts of a node into which the tested node was merged by a choice as subsumers (maximum deterministic branch tag 0 still accepts concepts with tag 0); it now accepts none of them in that case (cgc-o4).

Fixed. The classification of three small random ontologies from the differential fuzzing of the completion graph caching (cgc-fz-611, cgc-fz-620, cgc-fz-890 in Tests/cases/cgc-fuzz-known) did not terminate in some configurations. The process spun at 100 percent CPU with constant memory in CCalculationTableauCompletionTaskHandleAlgorithm::mergeMergingIndividualNodes. The at-most rule keeps the ids of the successors that are known to be distinct, and the successors that still have to be merged. When a successor is merged away, its link is removed and a link to the merge target is added, so the link count stays the same and the counters that decide whether the stored ids are still valid stayed balanced. The stale id was never replaced by its merge target, the lookup of its link returned null and the loop over the distinct set did not advance. The candidates are now verified against the links (countMergedAwayMergingCandidates) and the distinct set is relocated whenever it is not empty, not only when the counters are unbalanced. The relocation collects the stale ids before it changes the set. The configuration dependence of the original hangs came from the order in which nodes were merged.

Open. Deterministic wrong classification answers of fuzz ontologies (completion graph caching on and off give the same answer, HermiT and FaCT++ disagree): cgc-fz-3203 misses T5 below T4 (also in the direct satisfiability test of T5 and not T4). Fixed: cgc-fz-2462 (a second local copy of a node that is its own role successor in the qualification branches of an at-most restriction), cgc-fz-2029 (the backend cache synchronisation of a node that represents a nominal only through a non-deterministic merge used the deterministic base dependency, so a clash with the expanded role assertions skipped the other alternatives) and cgc-fz-3208 (the pseudo-model pretest of the classifier took a missing internal consequence of the subsumer as proof of a non-subsumption although the model of the subsumed class contained the subsumer itself). cgc-fz-2351 is not a Konclude error: T2 is satisfiable (FaCT++, JFact and an explicit model agree), the expectation came from an inconsistent HermiT answer.

Open. cgc-fz-2056 derives the extra C0 below C3 in some runs and not in others, with and without completion graph caching (minimal shape: C1 = {a4, a1}, (some r1.C1) below C1, C1 below (=1 r0.C3), C0 below (at least 2 r1.C1), r0 functional, r0(a3, a1), C0(a3); C0 is not below C3 since a4 can be an instance of C0 outside C3). With AllowBackendNeighbourExpansionBlocking=false the answer is always correct. Fixed: cgc-fz-3397 (since the existential rule builds the link to a nominal successor of an incompletely handled individual) and cgc-fz-3229 (since the backend cache synchronisation of a node that represents a nominal only through a non-deterministic merge uses the dependency of the merge).

Fixed. The classification of cgc-fz-3241 (both configurations) and cgc-fz-3344 (with completion graph caching) segfaulted in CIndividualIdentifier::getIndividualID() called from visitIndividualsRelevantMergingsBackendSynchronisationDataIndividuals. The test node was merged with a nominal into a new empty node (getIntoEmptyMergedIndividualNode), which is created with the nominal node type before the merge; mergeIndividualNodeInto only set the nominal individual for a target that was not yet a nominal node, so the new node received the merging hash and the backend cache synchronisation data of the nominal but no nominal individual, and the synchronisation dereferenced it. mergeIndividualNodeInto now sets the nominal individual whenever the target has none. Reduced reproducer: Tests/cases/dl/merged-nominal-empty-node-ontology.owl.xml.

Fixed. Fuzz ontologies on which the classification did not terminate. cgc-fz-2420 and cgc-fz-3122 hung in both configurations until the existential rule stopped accepting a cached neighbour of an incompletely handled individual for a successor integrated into a nominal. cgc-fz-3016, cgc-fz-2042 and cgc-fz-2078 hung because the qualification branches of an at-most restriction localized the processed node a second time when it was its own role successor; the second local copy replaced the first one and the at-most merging continued on the replaced copy (getLocalizedIndividual now always continues from the newest version of a node). cgc-fz-3310 and cgc-fz-2245 (whose classification without caching then still had a redundant direct edge below owl:Thing) hung because a successor recorded as distinct by the at-most merging was pruned when its creator was merged away; the repair of the distinct nodes replaced the missing id by the node itself, the dead id stayed in the set and the scan over the set did not advance. A pruned successor is now removed from the distinct nodes.

Fixed. Konclude answered consistent for cgc-fz-2167-ontology.owl.xml, which is inconsistent: C2 = {a0}, C0 = {a2}, C2 is below (some inverse r0.C0) so a2 r0 a0, C0 is below (all r0.C3) so a0 is in C3, and a0 is in C1 while C1 is disjoint with C3. Minimal shape: C0 below {a2}, C0 below (all r0.C3), C0(a2), (some inverse r0.C0)(a0), not-C3(a0). The individual saturation integrates the successor of the existential into the nominal a2 and records a2 as cached neighbour of a0, but it does not propagate the universal restriction of a2 back to a0 and marks a0 as not completely handled. The completion rule for existentials then found the cached neighbour a2 with C0 and accepted it as witness, so the link a2 r0 a0 was never built and the clash never derived (with and without completion graph caching). The cached-neighbour shortcut of the existential rule is now skipped when the saturation integrated the successor into a nominal and the association of the individual is not completely handled; the following nominal branch builds the link. The shortcut stays for all other cases (on roberts-family all of its hits are kept).
